text: On XX/XX/2023, I noticed a large check ( {$27000.00} ) had cleared that day through my bank, XXXX XXXX XXXX. When I clicked on the check, I did not recognize the recipient or the address. Then I noticed the font was changed. I immediately realized this check was changed and forged and deposited into a Wells Fargo bank in Pennsylvania. No account number was written on the back of the check. Realizing this check was deposited less than 24 hours prior, I emailed my Personal Business Banker at XXXX and called their Fraud Department to report this. The Fraud Department told me I needed to complete several pages of paperwork, which they will mail to me. I completed it all and immediately faxed it back to XXXX. I felt that valuable time was lost. I feel this would have been quickly settled had they only contacted Wells Fargo the day the check cleared in my account. At least they could have warned Wells Fargo that an inquiry was being made. As of today, Wells Fargo has not answered the 2 attempts that XXXX made in contacting them regarding this claim. My company is too small to just let {$27000.00} get stolen when I check my account on a daily basis for fraud and theft. I filed a complaint on XX/XX/XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, Wells Fargo contacted XXXX and asked for information the same information that XXXX originally sent to Well Fargo. XXXX responded to this request on XX/XX/XXXX and sent them everything they requested. Wells Fargo followed up with 2 letters to me. These letters contain a phone number that does not work and the name XXXX XXXX When I get through to Wells Fargo on another phone number, no one has any idea who this XXXX XXXX is and needs a last name. Please help. How can a bank be so corrupt? Thank you
